model.pretrained_by: Microsoft (the WavLM x-vector recipe for speaker verification)
model.licence_note: model weights are MIT; the AUDIO is the AMI Meeting Corpus, CC-BY-4.0, and is what the attribution obligation attaches to

models_considered.note: the instrument selection, recorded so the choice can be argued with. The attempts below were made while developing this file; only the first one produced the committed numbers.

used.why: ungated, a pinned revision SHA, a single `transformers` class, and a published same-speaker threshold on its own model card that this file measures and reproduces

speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb.status: installed into the GPU venv and run once as a diagnostic on the headset channels; it showed the same weakness as WavLM at 1 s windows, which is what identified the LENGTH defect rather than the model
speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb.why_not_the_headline: speechbrain fetches its checkpoint at run time, so the weights cannot be pinned by revision SHA the way this project pins its inputs
speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb.install_note: speechbrain 1.1.2 needed torchaudio 2.6.0+cu124 (to match the existing torch 2.6.0+cu124) and requests; both went into the GPU venv, never into the repo's .venv

microsoft/wavlm-base-plus.why_not: the plain backbone has no x-vector head, and training one is out of scope for a measurement

microsoft/unispeech-sat-base-plus.why_not: a different pretraining with the same x-vector head, so it was the natural second instrument, but the time went into the controls instead

model_card_selfcheck.purpose: same-speaker distance on the model card's own example (Librispeech, speaker 1272); the card's same-speaker threshold is cosine similarity 0.86, i.e. distance 0.14

method.embedding_unit: the WHOLE annotated turn, embedded as one utterance with the model's own feature extractor (padding + attention mask)
method.preprocessor: the model's own preprocessor_config.json: do_normalize=false, return_attention_mask=true
method.populations: all_audible is the primary population; solo_only applies the F0 experiment's no-overlap rule and is much smaller

min_input_s_rationale.why: the x-vector head's TDNN convolutions need a minimum input length; below roughly 2 s the forward pass returns NaN or raises 'Kernel size can't be greater than actual input size'. Every utterance is padded to at least min_input_s with the attention mask keeping the padding out of the pooling.
min_input_s_rationale.measured_before_the_rule: 5 of the 394 boundary clips in an earlier run came back non-finite

method.padding: every utterance is padded to ONE length for the whole call (the longest in it, and never less than min_input_s) with the attention mask keeping the padding out of the pooling, so an embedding depends on its own audio and not on its batch

length_sweep.why: the embedding's discriminative power is a function of how much audio it is given; a 1.0 s window of speech is not enough for this model, and reporting one point of this curve without the curve would be a measurement reported as a property
length_sweep.headline_rule: the longest minimum in the sweep that still leaves every speaker with at least 20 turns, so the enrolment/test split is not degenerate; NOT the point with the largest separation

f0_doc_style.pooled_sigma_definition: root-mean-square of the per-speaker MAD sigmas -- the noise floor experiments/twospeaker_verify.py uses

same_speaker_control._note: the same-speaker control: distances between two turns of the SAME speaker. Any method must not fire on this population.

shuffled_label_null.method: speaker labels permuted over turns, per-speaker turn counts preserved, separation recomputed from scratch

description.time_reversed: the waveform reversed in time. If the separation survives, the measurement is about the VOICE, not about the temporal detail of the utterance.
description.gain_scaled: each turn multiplied by a log-uniform random gain in [0.1, 10]. This model's preprocessor has do_normalize=false, so gain is NOT normalised away by construction; this measures what it actually costs.
description.white_noise: each turn replaced by noise of the same length and RMS. There is no speaker in the audio at all, so any separation that survives here is an artefact.

definition.positive: consecutive annotated turns with DIFFERENT speakers
definition.negative_same_speaker: consecutive annotated turns with the SAME speaker
definition.negative_within_turn: one turn split in half (no change at all)
definition.score: cosine distance between the last clip before the boundary and the first clip after it
definition.clip_rule: the last/first BOUNDARY_W_S seconds of the turn, clipped to the turn when the turn is shorter

eer_vs_same_speaker.eer_definition: min over thresholds of max(miss_rate, false_alarm_rate)

eer_vs_same_speaker_and_within_turn.eer_definition: min over thresholds of max(miss_rate, false_alarm_rate)

eer_vs_same_speaker.eer_definition: min over thresholds of max(miss_rate, false_alarm_rate)

f0_baseline.note: the same boundaries, scored by |median f0 before - median f0 after| in Hz

shuffled_label_null.note: the boundary geometry and the scores are held fixed; only the speaker labels over the turns are permuted, so the hand-off / same-speaker classes are reassigned at random

constant_decision_always_change.note: predicting 'speaker changed' for every boundary scores EER 0.5 by construction. It is written down so the headline cannot be read without it.

constant_decision_always_same.note: the mirror image; also 0.5 by construction.

headset_channel_reference.role: channel-separated reference: one headset microphone per speaker, so speaker identity is separation of the recording, not an inference
